Zippest requires no account and contains no ads, tracking or analytics. The app holds the network permission but only uses it when you tap the version number to check for updates (GitHub Releases API) or open a project or licence link in your browser. Otherwise Zippest never uploads files, file names, passwords or usage data.

Browsing, compression, extraction, copying, moving, renaming, previewing and integrity checks all happen locally. Only when you choose Open with or Share does the selected file or a temporary grant go to the chosen system app.

All files access is used to browse and modify internal storage; the Storage Access Framework handles folders you pick; notifications, the foreground service and wake locks keep compression and extraction running with the screen off and show progress. None of these permissions are used for unrelated data collection.

Clipboard content is read only in extraction settings or when you tap the clipboard entry. Passwords may be kept in memory or in encrypted background task data and are never uploaded. The app does not monitor or record clipboard changes in the background.

Files moved to Trash, app settings, task history and encrypted credentials stay in the app’s local data area.
The Trash limit is 2 GB; the oldest records are removed first.
Note: uninstalling Zippest also deletes Trash — restore important files to another folder first.
You can restore or permanently delete items in Trash, or clear app data in system settings.
Compression and extraction use local open-source libraries. They only process files and archive formats on this device and cannot track you or collect data remotely.
This policy is effective from %1$s. If a future feature adds network access, cloud services or data collection, this policy will be updated. Reach the maintainers via GitHub Issues.

Archive tool: batch password extraction, quick extension rename, split volumes, Trash,\nbackground tasks and local archive handling — plus file browsing on the side.

Zippest stays offline; only tapping the version number to check for updates calls the GitHub Releases API to look up the latest version and download an installer.\nFiles, passwords and file names stay on this device. The network permission is listed under Settings → Apps → Zippest → Permissions.
Zippest uses the open-source components below. Copyright belongs to their authors;\ntheir licences govern the terms.
